analysis.investment_thesis: Aarti Industries is the worst kind of story for a GARP investor: a company that peaked in 2022 and is now in earnings freefall, yet trades at P/E 43x — implying a PEG north of 15. The growth story has broken down completely, and you are being asked to pay a premium price for a deteriorating business.
key_strengths: Revenue has still grown from INR 3,006 Cr (FY16) to INR 7,271 Cr (FY25), showing the underlying market opportunity in specialty chemicals is real
Debt/Equity of 0.70 is manageable and the balance sheet is not yet in distress
Positive OCF in all 5 years (INR 519–1,319 Cr range) provides some financial resilience
key_risks: Net profit has collapsed from the peak of INR 1,186 Cr (FY22) to INR 331 Cr in FY25 — a 72% decline in three years while the stock still commands P/E 43x
ROE of just 6.03% and ROCE of 6.32% mean the company is barely earning its cost of capital despite heavy capex (INR 1,300–1,400 Cr/year) — classic value destruction
EBITDA margin has contracted sharply: from INR 1,687 Cr (FY22) to INR 986 Cr (FY25) as Chinese competition and raw material pressures have not abated
red_flags: Earnings are going the wrong direction: INR 1,186 Cr → 545 → 416 → 331 Cr over four years — this is not a dip, this is a trend
EV/EBITDA of 18.4x and P/E of 43x are growth-company multiples for a business where earnings are down 72% from peak — the market is pricing in a recovery that has not materialised
Finance costs rose from INR 86 Cr (FY21) to INR 275 Cr (FY25) as capex was debt-funded, but returns have not followed
analysis.detailed_analysis: The cardinal Lynch rule is 'never fall in love with a story when the numbers stop working.' Aarti Industries had a brilliant story in FY22 (specialty chemicals as China+1 beneficiary), but the numbers have unraveled violently since. Net profit dropped from INR 1,186 Cr to INR 331 Cr across four years — a 72% earnings collapse — while the company continued to pour INR 1,300+ Cr annually into capex with almost no FCF to show for it. The market still prices it at P/E 43x, implying it expects a massive earnings rebound; yet operating margins are stuck at 8.8% and ROE is a miserable 6%.
